basis: Full-year 2026 values as they apply on the annual return (not the prorated July-December payroll values). BC, NL and PE changed mid-year; see their notes. The estimator models what payroll withholds under CRA T4127 (and Revenu Quebec's formulas for Quebec), using those full-year values: brackets, basic personal amounts, Canada employment amount, CPP/QPP and EI/QPIP credits, the Ontario surtax, Ontario Health Premium and Ontario and BC tax reductions. Credits claimed only on the annual return (Ontario LIFT, the low-income reductions of MB, NB, NL, NS and PE, and the NT and NU cost of living credits) are not modelled.
extensions: referenceCases[].externalCheckData: raw third-party table rows used by reference.py to build the externalCheck string.

federal.notes: Lowest rate and credit rate are 14% for all of 2026. No federal change in the July 1, 2026 edition. Base CPP employee rate is proposed to fall to 4.75% from January 1, 2027 (not 2026).

qpp.notes: Employee total rate fell from 6.40% (2025) to 6.30% (2026): base 5.40% to 5.30%.

AB.name: Alberta
AB.notes: Credits are at 8% (CRA K1P = 0.08 x TCP). A supplemental credit (CRA K5P) adds 25% of the amount by which 8% credits exceed 4,896 (credit amounts over 61,200), restoring 10%. An employee's BPA + CPP + EI amounts total about 27,400, so it never applies here and is left out.

BC.name: British Columbia
BC.notes: MID-YEAR CHANGE. Budget 2026 (February 17, 2026) raised the lowest rate and the credit rate from 5.06% to 5.60% for the whole 2026 tax year and the tax reduction credit from 575 to 690 (eliminated at net income 44,952). Payroll used 5.06%/575 for January-June and prorated 6.14%/805 for July-December; the values here are the annual-return ones (CRA 'Option 2').

MB.name: Manitoba
MB.notes: Brackets and BPA are not indexed. taxReduction encodes the non-refundable Manitoba Family Tax Benefit for a single person with no dependants: 10.8% x max(0, 2,065 - 9% of net income) = max(0, 223.02 - 0.00972 x NI); it reaches zero at net income 22,944. Not in payroll formulas; annual return only. Confirm on the 2026 MB428 when published. PLANNER CHANGE 2026-11-19: taxReduction set to null. The Manitoba Family Tax Benefit (researched as max 223.02, 0.972% over 0; see SOURCES.md for its confidence) is claimed on the annual return and is not part of payroll deductions, so it is not modelled.

NB.name: New Brunswick
NB.notes: taxReduction is the NB low-income tax reduction for a single person. ESTIMATED: 2025 basic amount 802 (half of the 1,604 two-person maximum) and 2025 threshold 21,919 (2024's 21,343 x 1.027), each indexed 2% for 2026; the 3% rate and the 2024 threshold are from prior-year NB428 forms recalled from memory. Annual return only. Confirm on the 2026 NB428. PLANNER CHANGE 2026-11-19: taxReduction set to null. The New Brunswick low-income tax reduction (researched as max 818, 3% over 22,357; see SOURCES.md for its confidence) is claimed on the annual return and is not part of payroll deductions, so it is not modelled.

NL.name: Newfoundland and Labrador
NL.notes: MID-YEAR CHANGE. Budget 2026 (April 29, 2026) raised the BPA; the 2026 annual amount is 13,094 (was 11,188; payroll used a prorated 15,000 for July-December, and 15,000 is expected to be the full amount from 2027). taxReduction is the NL low income tax reduction for a single person: 842 (Regulation 18/26) less 16% of net income over 24,191 (threshold from EY, secondary). Annual return only. PLANNER CHANGE 2026-11-19: taxReduction set to null. The Newfoundland and Labrador low income tax reduction (researched as max 842, 16% over 24,191; see SOURCES.md for its confidence) is claimed on the annual return and is not part of payroll deductions, so it is not modelled.

NS.name: Nova Scotia
NS.notes: BPA is a flat 11,932 (the income-tested supplement was removed in 2025). taxReduction is the NS low-income tax reduction for a single person (300 less 5% of net income over 15,000, gone at 21,000; range from EY, secondary; 300 basic amount inferred from the 2025 spouse amount and the range). Annual return only. PLANNER CHANGE 2026-11-19: taxReduction set to null. The Nova Scotia low-income tax reduction (researched as max 300, 5% over 15,000; see SOURCES.md for its confidence) is claimed on the annual return and is not part of payroll deductions, so it is not modelled.

NT.name: Northwest Territories
NT.notes: NOT MODELLED: the refundable NWT cost of living tax credit, claimed on the annual return (about 2.6% of the first 12,000 of adjusted net income, 1.25% of the next 36,000, 1% above 48,000, maximum about 942; figures recalled from prior years, not verified for 2026). It is not part of payroll deductions.

NU.name: Nunavut
NU.notes: NOT MODELLED: the refundable Nunavut cost of living tax credit, claimed on the annual return (about 2% of adjusted net income, maximum about 1,500; recalled from prior years, not verified for 2026). It is not part of payroll deductions.

ON.name: Ontario
ON.notes: healthPremium is the Ontario Health Premium split into additive steps (cumulative caps 300, 450, 600, 750, 900). NOT MODELLED: the non-refundable Low-Income Individuals and Families Tax (LIFT) credit (min(875, 5.05% of employment income) less 5% of net income over 32,500); it is claimed on the annual return and is not part of payroll deductions.

PE.name: Prince Edward Island
PE.notes: MID-YEAR CHANGE. Budget 2026 (April 14, 2026, corrected April 22) added a 20% bracket over 200,000 for the whole 2026 tax year (Bill 23; payroll used a prorated 21% for July-December). The fifth threshold is 142,520 per CRA and the PEI government; EY and TaxTips print 142,250. taxReduction is the PEI low-income tax reduction for a single person: 350 less 5% of net income over 23,000, gone at 30,000 (threshold from the PEI government; 350 and 5% from EY, secondary). Annual return only. PLANNER CHANGE 2026-11-19: taxReduction set to null. The Prince Edward Island low-income tax reduction (researched as max 350, 5% over 23,000; see SOURCES.md for its confidence) is claimed on the annual return and is not part of payroll deductions, so it is not modelled.

QC.name: Quebec
QC.notes: Quebec gives no credit for QPP, EI or QPIP employee contributions (they are built into the basic personal amount). Enhanced QPP contributions (first and second additional) are deductible, which section 4.4 already does through NI. employmentDeduction is the deduction for workers: 6% of work income, maximum 1,450 (maximum from Revenu Quebec; the 6% rate is the long-standing statutory rate, not restated on the 2026 page retrieved). Federal tax for Quebec residents uses QPP base 5.30%, EI 1.30% and QPIP credits and the 16.5% abatement.

SK.name: Saskatchewan
SK.notes: BPA includes the extra 500 a year on top of indexation.

YT.name: Yukon
YT.notes: BPA mirrors the federal amount including its phase-out (CRA: BPAYT mirrors BPAF); the Canada employment amount also applies at 6.4% (CRA K4P).
